title: Getting started
desc: Install from Steam, first launch, and the one-screen layout.
text: user guide / getting started getting started install from steam, first launch, and the one-screen layout. first launch install & first run ikandy is a windows desktop app, installed through steam. no account beyond steam, no setup wizard: you can be visualizing system audio in under a minute. install open ikandy on steam and install it like any other steam app. launch it from your steam library. steam keeps it updated automatically. on first launch ikandy indexes the preset library and runs a background reactivity scan. this takes a few seconds and happens silently while you use the app. a short welcome walks you in, a one-time photosensitivity notice shows before anything flashes, and the ? on the console replays the guided tour whenever you want it. what it needs windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), 8 gb ram, 2 gb of free storage, an audio output device, and a directx 12 gpu with webgpu support (nvidia gtx 900 series, amd rx 400 series, or intel uhd 600 and newer). core visual playback runs locally and does not require a separate ikandy account. steam is used for installation and licensing; optional features such as provider-based ai, online metadata, and enabled diagnostics require an internet connection. details are in the privacy policy . fastest path to visuals start playing music in any app on your computer, then in ikandy pick now playing as the source. no setup, no auth: ikandy listens to whatever windows is currently playing and starts reacting immediately. the layout one screen, one console ikandy has one layout: the full screen is the stage, and a slim console bar lives at the bottom. everything routes through that bar. when you step up to performing, stage is a second surface built for the job, and the main window always shows a return button when stage has control. the console bar, left to right now playing : album art, track title, artist. click the art to open synced lyrics. the source pill under the title shows what is connected; click it to change sources. playback : play, pause, skip, volume, and a seek bar. works with spotify, musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, and system audio, subject to each source's capabilities. engine + presets : tabs pick the engine that is driving the stage: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , or image . arrows step through looks, browse opens the full library, and auto cycles on a dwell timer you set. vibe + output : the vibe popover shapes bloom, motion blur, and post intensity. the scenes popover switches hand-built scenes with a per-scene intensity control. the master audio popover sets how much bass, mid, and treble drive the visuals, with a mix control, a master intensity fader, and a god-rays toggle. output opens the logo overlay , and the lut control can auto-pick a color grade per scene or cycle grades per preset. view + settings : fullscreen, hide the console, the black or chrome theme, a knobs / sliders switch for how the board's controls render, multi-monitor output, and the gear for sources & settings. the ? replays the guided tour any time. popovers, not buried menus deep controls live in small popovers that open from the bar: vibe, scenes, master audio, and luts. the gear opens the one real modal, sources & settings , for connecting sources, themes, ui size, displays, and diagnostics. live level meters sit on the board itself so you can see the signal you are mixing. multi-monitor extra displays are outputs you route to. the output window can mirror the main view onto the displays you pick, each mirror with its own gain, or span one continuous canvas edge to edge across them (the titlebar hides so nothing interrupts the image). per-display checkboxes choose which monitors take part, and live wallpaper can claim any of them as a set-and-forget desktop. the tour is always current the app's built-in tour (the ? on the console) walks these zones live, on your build. if this page and your console ever disagree, trust the console. next → audio sources + controls

title: Audio sources + controls
desc: Now Playing, Spotify, MusicBee, foobar2000, VLC, per-app capture with Smart Auto, shuffle, and playlists.
text: user guide / audio sources + controls audio sources + controls now playing, spotify, musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, per-app capture with smart auto, shuffle, and playlists. audio sources connect your music ikandy can connect to five source modes. each one offers a different feature set depending on what its underlying api exposes. switching between them automatically pauses the previous one. 🎵 spotify ● works out of the box · no account connection spotify plays through windows media controls, the same lane as any modern media app. press play in spotify and ikandy picks up track info, album art when the app publishes it, and the transport controls windows exposes: play, pause, and skip. per-process capture can lock the visuals onto spotify's audio alone. there is nothing to connect: no sign-in, no developer app, no keys. ikandy has no spotify account integration; it reads what spotify publishes to windows on your machine. followed an older guide? earlier builds offered a separate spotify connection with a client id setup. that integration has been removed. nothing is required from you: play in spotify and ikandy follows automatically. 🐝 musicbee ● full features · mbxhub plugin connects through the user-installed mbxhub plugin. ikandy can read now-playing metadata and artwork, control playback, browse playlists, search, and use musicbee's shuffle and repeat modes. one-time setup download mbxhub from the official musicbee add-on page . extract the download and copy mb_mbxhub.dll and mbxhub.exe into musicbee's plugins folder. restart musicbee, then confirm mbxhub appears under edit → preferences → plugins . in ikandy, choose musicbee . leave host at 127.0.0.1 and port at 8080 unless you changed the mbxhub configuration, then click connect . connection check with musicbee and mbxhub running, open http://localhost:8080/docs . if the api documentation loads, the plugin is reachable; use the configured port if you changed it. plugin status mbxhub is currently published by its developer as release-candidate software. the plugin requires .net framework 4.8, and its companion shell requires the .net 8 desktop runtime. its api or setup may change; the official add-on page is authoritative. 🎧 foobar2000 ● full features · beefweb plugin for the audiophile crowd. connects via the foo_beefweb component: a rest/json api that exposes the full library. playlist browse with search, every shuffle mode foobar supports, transport, album art, lyrics. the most feature-complete source ikandy offers. one-time setup download and install foo_beefweb from github.com/hyperblast/beefweb/releases . in foobar2000: file → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control . tick enable http server (default port 8880 ). optionally set a password. click apply. in ikandy, choose foobar2000 , leave port at 8880 , enter the password if set, and click connect . foobar2000 → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control 📺 vlc ● standard · local http connects to vlc’s built-in web interface: play, pause, skip, shuffle on/off, album art, synced lyrics. no library browse; pick what to play in vlc, control playback in ikandy. one-time setup open vlc → tools → preferences . switch show settings to all . navigate to interface → main interfaces and tick web . expand main interfaces → lua , set a lua http password , and save. restart vlc. in ikandy, choose vlc , paste the password, and click connect . vlc → preferences → all → interface → main interfaces → web (ticked) custom port if port 8080 is taken, change it in the same vlc preferences pane. match it in ikandy's vlc settings. 🎙️ now playing ● basic · windows media controls · zero setup the general windows source. reads compatible apps that publish to windows media controls, including spotify, youtube music, apple music, browser tabs, and tidal. track info, available transport controls, and album art (when the app publishes it) follow the active source. no browse, no shuffle. how to use it start playing music in any app on your computer. in ikandy, click the source pill on the console and pick now playing . track info and transport light up within a second. ikandy shows or greys out individual buttons based on what the active source app actually supports. firefox needs a flag chrome and edge bridge html5 media session to windows media controls automatically. firefox doesn’t by default : open about:config , search media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled , set it to true , and restart firefox. 🎯 per-process capture ● audio isolation · settings → source capture audio from one specific app rather than the whole system mix. if you’re gaming while listening through spotify or musicbee, ikandy normally reacts to everything: game effects, discord pings, notification sounds, and music. per-process capture can lock on to the music app alone. how to use it start the app you want to capture (for example, spotify or musicbee) and play something. in ikandy, open settings (⚙) → source tab → per-process capture . click scan . ikandy lists every app currently producing audio, with its icon. click capture next to the app you want. the banner at the top of the section confirms which app is active. to stop, click stop in the banner. ikandy returns to system audio automatically. switching apps click capture on a different app while one is already active : ikandy switches cleanly with no confirmation dialog. the banner updates immediately. use cases react to spotify or musicbee only, ignoring game audio and discord capture a daw or audio editor output for a live mix visualization isolate browser tab audio when youtube is playing alongside other apps test a specific app’s audio routing without affecting the rest of the system requires a connected source first per-process capture shares the same audio graph as system audio. connect a supported source (spotify, musicbee, vlc, etc.) or click 🎤 reconnect audio once before using it: this initializes the audio context. after that, per-process capture works independently. one tab runs the connections connect, disconnect, and switch available sources from ⚙ → source : musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, spotify and other media apps through windows media controls, browser and system audio, plus the system-audio reconnect and your playlists. a source that still needs setup shows it on its row and routes you to the right place with one click. transport buttons a source cannot perform (some apps do not expose skip or seek) grey out with a hint instead of failing silently. and if you just have a file: drag an audio file onto ikandy and it plays it, no source setup at all. audio controls beyond picking a source, you shape how the audio drives the visuals. bass / mid / treble drive : boost or cut how much the low, mid, and high frequencies push the visuals, plus a mix control to blend. master intensity : one fat fader for overall visual intensity on the current engine, from calm to double strength. per-asset reactivity : each asset (like a logo overlay) has its own master audio-reactivity control. volume and transport : play, pause, skip, and volume for sources that support control. drop a file : drag a local audio file onto ikandy and it plays and visualizes it directly. shuffle + playlists shuffle follows the source. musicbee and foobar2000 expose their own shuffle, repeat, and playback-order modes, and the playlist panel loads supported-source playlists with search, so you can browse and play without leaving the visuals. apps that ride windows media controls, spotify included, keep their shuffle settings inside the app itself. ← previous getting started next → visualizers + presets

title: Visualizers + presets
desc: Five engines on one stage. The MilkDrop library, cycling, reactivity, and your own presets.
text: user guide / visualizers + presets visualizers + presets five engines on one stage. the milkdrop library, cycling, reactivity, and your own presets. visualizers five engines, one stage the engine tabs on the console pick what is driving the stage: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , or image . milkdrop is the deep preset library this page covers; glsl and webgpu run hand-built and imported scenes , spout turns a live feed into a source, and image layers fx shaders over a photo. milkdrop, reborn the milkdrop engine is built on butterchurn, a webgl port of the legendary milkdrop visualizer. ikandy ships a deep preset library: the base collection, extra curated packs, and an image category that layers especially well over a background photo. cycling looks auto on the console cycles presets on a dwell timer you set: how many seconds each look holds before the next. the sliders icon next to it opens timing and blend controls; a longer blend morphs cinematically between looks, a short one cuts kinetic. auto-cycle draws from a shuffle bag, so every preset in the active pool plays once before any can repeat. reactivity on first launch ikandy quietly scores the library in the background while you use the app, classifying each preset as reactive, non-reactive, or image-texture. the results are cached. in the browser, the reactive filter narrows the pool to presets that visibly answer the music; if the scan has not finished, a run scan button is right there. there is also a reactivity master for the whole engine: turn it down and presets settle into calm ambient motion instead of going dark, turn it up and the beat drives harder. the browser browse opens the full library with thumbnails. hover any card for a live preview; click to load it on the stage immediately. scene cards preview from a cached clip the same way. tabs, favorites, hiding, flagging, and reordering are covered in library . your own presets in the browser, custom presets loads a folder of converted butterchurn json presets , merged alongside the bundled library and remembered across restarts. butterchurn uses a json preset format rather than milkdrop's original .milk binaries; if a folder contains .milk files, ikandy says so and points you at the converter. misbehaving presets some presets produce invalid values on modern gpus. ikandy skips broken or near-black presets automatically and remembers them, so the cycle keeps moving. anything questionable lands in the flagged tab for you to judge. ← previous audio sources + controls next → library: browse + manage

title: Library: browse + manage
desc: Nine tabs, search, maker pills, favorites, hide and flag, My Scenes, previews, saving, file types.
text: user guide / library: browse + manage library: browse + manage nine tabs, search, maker pills, favorites, hide and flag, my scenes, previews, saving, file types. one browser, nine tabs every visual in ikandy lives in one browser. the top tabs split it by kind, each with its own identity color: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , and images for your picture library, then my scenes for the things you have made, and the three curation tabs: favorites , hidden , flagged . find it fast search filters the grid as you type, with a one-tap clear. category tabs inside milkdrop narrow the pool: all, reactive (from the reactivity scan ), your custom presets, and more. maker pills filter milkdrop by preset author with one click; glsl and webgpu get the same artist pills for their scenes. random pulls one look from the current pool and drops you straight back on the stage. three densities : list, grid, and large. large keeps cards big enough to actually read. curate it star anything : every card carries a favorite star, the favorites tab and its count update live, and shuffle can be told to draw from favorites only. hide what you never want in rotation; flag what needs a second look. both get their own tabs, so nothing is ever lost. drag to reorder : every grid in the browser reorders by drag, and your order sticks. previews hover any milkdrop card and it live-renders in a preview popup. scene cards on the visual, webgpu, and spout tabs play a cached clip on hover instead, so previews stay instant. click any card to put it on the stage immediately. my scenes scenes you compose or generate land in my scenes. each card can be replayed, renamed, or deleted. imported presets start as pending; promote the keepers into your own custom category with one action. saving, editing, versions from the studio, save as new creates a fresh asset and overwrite updates the one you are editing. originals and templates are protected: they can only be saved as new, never overwritten, and a duplicate-name guard keeps two assets from colliding. file types the image library accepts png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, and svg, and feeds both backgrounds and the logo maker . shaders paste in as glsl or wgsl text, milkdrop presets load as converted butterchurn json (the app detects .milk files and points you at the converter), and ai scenes travel as .vis packages with their provenance intact. browse music and visuals together the sync button opens the preset browser and the playlist panel as a pair, so you can line up the next track and the next look side by side. ← previous visualizers + presets next → scenes

title: Scenes
desc: The hand-built scene library and how scenes differ from presets.
text: user guide / scenes scenes the hand-built scene library and how scenes differ from presets. custom scenes audio-reactive, built in-house scenes are direct audio-reactive engines written for ikandy, driven by real-time frequency analysis. where a milkdrop preset interprets a recipe of math, a scene is code that listens: the music literally makes the picture. a library across four runtimes the scene library has grown far past its first handful, and it spans four runtimes: glsl fragment scenes, canvas2d scenes, three.js scenes, and webgpu compute scenes when your gpu supports them. the range runs from classic spectrum work (flames, bars, sweeping rays) to deep-space flythroughs, gravitational lenses, particle trails, and heavy compute pieces. flight scenes even take a game controller: plug one in and fly . turning scenes on open the scenes popover from the console and pick a card; it plays immediately. every scene has an intensity control for how hard it answers the audio, and scenes that need more expose their own row of controls right there: tone knobs, a god-rays switch, a color-grade slot. the house rule audio drives light and color, never the camera. nothing on screen shakes to the beat; when a scene has a camera, it belongs to you or the autopilot. it is why ikandy stays watchable for hours. layering scenes sit over the milkdrop stage and over fx images. drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover to let a scene take center stage, or keep it high and blend the two. scenes and fx shaders run at the same time. make your own scenes you compose, import, or generate with ai land in my scenes , ready to replay, rename, or put in a rundown. ← previous library: browse + manage next → fx shaders

title: FX shaders
desc: Real-time post effects and the FX image pipeline.
text: user guide / fx shaders fx shaders real-time post effects and the fx image pipeline. fx real-time fx shaders fx is three layers deep in ikandy: living treatments over an image, a post chain over everything, and a play layer for your hands. fx images pick a background photo on the image engine and run a live treatment over it. the set covers weather and texture (rain, fog, heat haze, dust film), analog and broadcast decay (vhs warp, data corruption, hologram), and paint and material (ink bleed, watercolor, liquid metal, shatter, plasma arc). every treatment is audio-aware, and the library keeps growing. the post chain a multi-pass post chain runs over the whole show: bloom, chromatic aberration, grain, scanlines, vignette, and contrast, each on a live knob with its own status light, plus tone and lut color grading and a god-rays pass. beat-reactive particle bursts ride on top as their own layer. this is the finish that makes everything underneath read like one image. the play layer mouse fx and draw mode put the pointer in the show: click ripples, freehand drawing with adjustable width, and particle trails, all blended over the visuals without ever touching the camera. performance quality tiers (battery, standard, high, ultra) scale the render resolution and supersampling, so the same show runs right on a laptop on battery and on a desktop pushing a wall. ← previous scenes next → spout in + out

title: Spout in + out
desc: Publish visuals to OBS and VJ software, or post-process compatible feeds.
text: user guide / spout in + out spout in + out publish visuals to obs and vj software, or post-process compatible feeds. spout a node in the rig spout is a gpu texture-sharing workflow for compatible windows apps. ikandy supports spout input and output. spout out: publish the show turn on spout output in sources & settings, give the sender a name, and ikandy can appear as a source in compatible receivers such as obs, resolume, touchdesigner, madmapper, and vmix. the output is the composited visual feed; the console and panels are designed to stay out of it. output performance depends on your hardware, scene, resolution, and the receiving application. you can keep working in other apps while the feed runs. overlays on the broadcast two switches decide what rides on everything you broadcast, the second screen and spout and recordings alike: the now playing card and lyrics . one switch per overlay, so a clean feed is one click away. spout in: post-process a compatible feed pipe a live feed into ikandy from a compatible spout sender such as obs, touchdesigner, resolume, or madmapper: pick the sender in source → spout in , choose a frame rate up to 60, and use the feed as a source. the browser's spout tab contains scenes built for live feeds. tier note spout output ships in the studio tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous fx shaders next → wallpaper + displays

title: Wallpaper + displays
desc: Any visual behind your icons. Mirror or Span, per display, survives Explorer restarts.
text: user guide / wallpaper + displays wallpaper + displays any visual behind your icons. mirror or span, per display, survives explorer restarts. set the desktop as your stage live wallpaper runs the visual behind your desktop icons while you work, on any mix of displays, driven by whatever ikandy is listening to. it is a set-and-forget output: open sources & settings → live wallpaper , click a display to toggle it on, and get back to work. change the visual any time from the console or stage and the desktop follows. the wallpaper survives explorer restarts, and it keeps rendering even when the main ikandy window is covered or minimized. fit mode: mirror or span mirror (the default) puts the same feed on each screen you picked. span stretches one image across all attached displays as a single canvas; it needs two or more screens, and it takes over the routing while it is on. both modes persist. the output window separate from wallpaper, the output window is a broadcast surface: mirror the main view onto the displays you choose, each mirror with its own gain, or span one continuous visual edge to edge (the titlebar hides so nothing interrupts the image). right-click the fullscreen button for a quick "send to a second screen" chooser. add hide-ui mode and the pixels are all that is left. overlays the now playing card and lyrics each have a broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings, or keep every output clean. good to know toggle wallpaper off any time from the same panel if anything misbehaves. performance cost scales with the visual you pick. calm scenes cost very little; heavy compute scenes cost more. tier note desktop wallpaper ships in the pro tier, on any number of displays and in both fit modes. the output window on a single screen is also pro. spanning one visual across multiple monitors, or running mirrors on several screens at once, ships in the studio tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous spout in + out next → lyrics

title: Lyrics
desc: Synced lyrics on screen, where they come from, and what to do when a track has none.
text: user guide / lyrics lyrics synced lyrics on screen, where they come from, and what to do when a track has none. lyrics words on the show synced lyrics ride the visuals, line by line, timed to the track. click the album art on the console to open them; click again to put them away. three modes classic draws the current line clean over the show. physics hands each line to a physics simulation, so words drift, swing, and settle with their own weight. make them yours position the line at the top, center, or bottom of the stage, scale the font from subtle to headline, set the opacity, and pick a color: the theme accent, white, or a swatch of your own. where the words come from ikandy reads lyrics from your own files, matched by the artist and title of the playing track: a synced .lrc file saved next to the track, or one in your linked lyrics folder. synced files scroll in time with the music; plain text shows as static lyrics. if no local file matches, ikandy shows nothing instead of guessing, which is where the next part comes in. add your own: tap to time open add lyrics and paste the words. if they already carry timestamps, they play immediately. if they are plain text, tap to time turns timing them into a performance: play the track and stamp each line the moment it lands. seekable sources get a small timeline with previous, play, and next, so a missed stamp is a two-second fix, not a restart. saved lyrics live in your local lyrics folder, keyed by title and artist, and you can point ikandy at a folder of your own. on the broadcast lyrics have their own broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings , or keep the output clean. tier note physics lyrics and the tap-to-time editor ship in the pro tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous wallpaper + displays next → stage: perform

title: STAGE: perform
desc: Now/Next decks, GO with crossfades, blackout and strobe, pads, rundowns, shows, combos.
text: user guide / stage: perform stage: perform now/next decks, go with crossfades, blackout and strobe, pads, rundowns, shows, combos. the console you perform from stage is the live view: a broadcast desk for planning a night and steering it in real time. when stage is live, the main window shows a return button so you always know which surface has control. now, next, go two decks with live previews: now is what the room sees, next is what you have lined up. click next to pick a look from the library, long-press to grab whatever is currently playing, right-click to clear. hit go and next takes the stage with a real crossfade: the outgoing frame freezes and dissolves into the incoming look, so transitions read as intentional, never as a cut. hold pins the current look against the autopilot. ride the moment a row of momentary performance keys sits under your fingers: blackout , a beat-locked strobe (hard photosensitive-safety cap of three flashes per second), and freeze . press and hold; release and the show returns. every stage control carries an address, so all of it lands on midi and osc . pads hot-cue pads hold looks you want on a trigger, each with a live thumbnail. assign a pad, hit it when the room needs it. rundowns, plans, pools, autopilot build a rundown for the night: concrete entries play a specific look with its own duration, pool entries shuffle from a group you curated. reorder by drag; unset entries flag themselves so nothing surprises you mid-set. autopilot follows the rundown, or smart-shuffles when none is loaded, with a dwell you pick from seconds to minutes and a live countdown to the next switch. shows new / save / load / delete manage whole shows: a saved show carries the rundown, your pads, and the per-output setup, so friday's rig comes back with one load. combos the combos tab is a layer compositor with a live preview: stack looks into a composite, save it, and recall the whole stack in one click. tempo and the logo tap four or more times to set the bpm by feel; double-click to clear it. the logo button opens the image studio to build or edit your overlay and lights up whenever one is live. outputs route per screen, so the projector and the stream can carry different dressing. stage ships in the studio tier. tier contents at launch are listed on the pricing page ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous lyrics next → logo maker

title: Logo maker
desc: Image Studio: text or image, chrome and matte finishes, live on any visual.
text: user guide / logo maker logo maker image studio: text or image, chrome and matte finishes, live on any visual. image studio: make the logo the logo maker builds a broadcast-style overlay that rides on top of any running visual: your name, your mark, live on the output. create start from text or bring an image from your library. a studio preview backdrop helps you judge it, and it is preview only: your logo stays transparent and the backdrop is never baked into the asset. finishes two live material finishes ship today: chrome , liquid metal that catches the scene, and black , a matte powder-coat. each asset also carries its own audio-reactivity control, so the logo can breathe with the music or hold still. save and apply apply live puts it on the output immediately. save as new keeps a version; originals and templates are protected from overwrite. on stage, the logo button opens the studio directly and lights up whenever an overlay is live, so you always know it is on. ← previous stage: perform next → midi, phone remote, gamepad

title: MIDI, phone remote, gamepad
desc: Bind hardware with MIDI Learn, steer from your phone over LAN, fly with a controller.
text: user guide / midi, phone remote, gamepad midi, phone remote, gamepad bind hardware with midi learn, steer from your phone over lan, fly with a controller. hands on the rig three ways to drive ikandy without touching the mouse: hardware midi, your phone, and a game controller. midi learn click midi learn , then move a control on your hardware. that knob or fader is now bound. bindings can be exported and imported as json, so a rig setup travels with you. bound controls tick green so you can see the mapping land. osc stage carries an osc receiver: switch it on, set the port, and send. every stage control has a stable address (strobe, blackout, go, pads, and the rest), so lighting desks and show controllers speak to ikandy the same way your hardware does. phone remote (lan) start the phone remote and a phone on your local network can steer the show from its browser. this is intended for a trusted lan, not direct internet exposure. use the source-ip allowlist on shared or untrusted networks; leave it empty only when you intend to accept all local senders. gamepad flight flight scenes accept a controller with zero setup: plug one in and any input takes the controls. left stick steers, right stick looks, right trigger throttle, left trigger brake. hands off for five seconds and the autopilot resumes; tab or the b button hands back instantly. the mouse never touches the camera, it belongs to the ui. midi and osc control ship in the studio tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous logo maker next → ai scene generation

title: AI scene generation
desc: Bring your own key. Generate, fix, and tune scenes with a supported provider.
text: user guide / ai scene generation ai scene generation bring your own key. generate, fix, and tune scenes with a supported provider. an ai that writes scenes ikandy can generate new visual scenes with ai, and can repair or tune imported shaders in the ai shader studio. it is bring-your-own-key: you connect an account from a supported provider and pay that provider directly. ikandy does not sell separate ai credits. your key stays yours the credential is stored using the operating system's secure storage. ikandy uses it to authenticate requests to the provider you choose; provider terms and data handling apply. what it can do generate : describe a look and get a runnable scene. ai fix : paste a shader that will not compile and let the sandbox suggest a repair after a compile check. ai tune : ask for adjustments to a working scene, in plain language. costs provider charges, availability, and estimates can change. review the estimate shown in ikandy and your provider's terms before you submit a job. guided ai scene generation ships in the pro tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous midi, phone remote, gamepad next → controls, themes, tips

title: Controls, themes, tips
desc: Reactivity, seek and volume, three theme layers, UI size, workflow tips.
text: user guide / controls, themes, tips controls, themes, tips reactivity, seek and volume, three theme layers, ui size, workflow tips. controls & themes tune the whole thing the console is the control surface; this page is the small print around it. reactivity, everywhere it matters every engine carries a reactivity control: turn it down and the visuals settle into calm ambient motion, turn it up and they snap to the beat. the master audio popover goes further with bass, mid, and treble drive , a mix control, and the master intensity fader. sensible defaults sit in the middle and work for most music. the seek bar the progress bar in the playback zone is draggable: click and drag anywhere on it to seek, on every source that supports seeking. volume lives right next to it for sources that allow control; anything that does not is greyed with a hint, not hidden. three layers of theme console material : black , a matte powder-coat, or chrome , liquid metal with dark text. the whole board, browser, and playlist panel change together. accent color : swatches like gold, neon, forest, ember, lavender, and crimson, plus a custom picker and a random that surprises you. the accent runs through every knob, tab, and led. panel background : schemes including slate and the light cloud, plus a panel opacity slider so the chrome can float over the show as much or as little as you like. add the knobs / sliders switch for how the board's controls render, and a ui size setting for readability at couch distance. themes change the chrome, never the visuals. set it once, forget it everything persists across sessions: reactivity, theme, accent, source preferences, custom preset folders, the last-used look. close it, reopen it, it is your rig. workflow tips spotlight a scene or image : drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover to 30 to 50 percent and let the layer underneath breathe through. scenes and fx shaders run at the same time. for recording or streaming : classic lyric mode over a clean scene with a subtle analog fx reads beautifully on video, and the broadcast overlay switches keep the feed intentional. lyrics need honest metadata : correct artist and title fetch the right words. if lyrics look wrong, check the tags on the playing source first. ← previous ai scene generation next → troubleshooting + help

title: Troubleshooting + help
desc: Fixes for the common snags, and where to reach a human.
text: user guide / troubleshooting + help troubleshooting + help fixes for the common snags, and where to reach a human. troubleshooting when things get weird the most common issues people run into, and how to fix them. click any item to expand. now playing says "nothing is playing" windows reports no app is currently registered as the smtc owner. simply start playing music in any app and the message will disappear within a second. if music is playing and now playing still doesn’t see it: firefox : open about:config , set media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled to true , restart firefox. chrome / edge : check chrome://flags for hardware media key handling and set it to enabled . apple music for windows : can be inconsistent. try pausing/resuming, or use a dedicated source instead. now playing controls grey out / next or previous don't work by design. ikandy queries the active app for which transport commands it actually exposes: some apps (single youtube videos, podcasts) don’t advertise next or previous, so ikandy locks those buttons. hover any greyed-out button to see the reason. for broader transport controls, connect a dedicated source such as musicbee, foobar2000, or vlc, or play in an app that publishes full controls to windows media controls. "could not start audio source" / no audio reactivity windows treats system audio capture the same as microphone access for privacy purposes. fix: settings → privacy & security → microphone → toggle let desktop apps access your microphone on. restart ikandy. if that doesn’t help, click 🎤 reconnect audio in settings (⚙) → source tab . spotify: which controls work? spotify plays through windows media controls. play, pause, and skip work when spotify publishes them; some controls (seek, volume, shuffle) live inside spotify itself. there is no sign-in and no account connection: press play in spotify and ikandy follows. if you followed an older guide that asked for a client id and a spotify developer app, that connection has been removed from ikandy. no setup is needed anymore. vlc won't connect open http://localhost:8080 in a browser: you should see the vlc web ui password prompt. if you don't, the web interface isn't enabled. fix: vlc → tools → preferences → show settings: all → interface → main interfaces → tick web . expand lua below it and confirm a lua http password is set. restart vlc. foobar2000 won't connect in foobar2000 → file → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control , confirm enable http server is ticked. test by visiting http://localhost:8880 in a browser. if you see the beefweb player, the plugin is healthy. if you set a password, paste it exactly as configured in ikandy's foobar2000 settings. musicbee won't connect confirm musicbee is running and that mbxhub appears under edit → preferences → plugins . the mbxhub bundle's mb_mbxhub.dll and mbxhub.exe should be in musicbee's plugins folder. test by visiting http://localhost:8080/docs in a browser. if the mbxhub api documentation loads, match ikandy's host and port to the plugin configuration. the ikandy defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 8080 . if the plugin does not load, confirm .net framework 4.8 and the .net 8 desktop runtime are available, then check the official mbxhub requirements and installation notes . install or update problems through steam steam handles installing and updating ikandy. if an install stalls or a launch fails after an update, use steam's built-in repair: right-click ikandy in your library, then properties → installed files → verify integrity of game files . why doesn't ikandy react only to spotify or musicbee when i'm playing a game? by default ikandy captures the entire system audio mix: game sound effects, discord calls, notification pings, and music all go in together. the visualizer reacts to whichever is loudest at any given moment, which is often the game. fix: use per-process capture. open settings (⚙) → source tab → per-process capture , click scan , then click capture next to spotify or musicbee. ikandy will focus on that app's audio stream while the game keeps running normally. visuals don't react to my music confirm the source is connected: the console bar's now playing zone should show the track name and source. visuals react to system audio regardless of which source you’ve picked for track info. if the visualizer is static while music plays, audio isn’t reaching ikandy. click 🎤 reconnect audio in settings (⚙) → source tab , and check windows microphone permissions. i have 5.1 or 7.1 surround sound and the visuals barely move ikandy captures a stereo loopback stream. with 5.1/7.1 configured, windows mixes most music into rear/centre/sub channels, leaving the front l/r that ikandy captures very quiet. fix: set your default output to stereo (2 channel) : right-click speaker icon → sounds → playback tab. right-click your active output → configure speakers → choose stereo . right-click again → properties → advanced → pick a 2-channel format from default format . apply, then in ikandy hit 🎤 reconnect audio in settings (⚙) → source tab . lyrics aren't showing up lyrics load from your own files, matched by the artist and title of the playing track: a synced .lrc next to the track, or one in your linked lyrics folder. if no local file matches, ikandy shows nothing instead of guessing. use add lyrics and tap to time to create one; see the lyrics guide . also check: if your files have incorrect artist/title tags, the match can land on the wrong song. performance is choppy or stuttering ikandy is gpu-bound. if your gpu is busy with another task, frame rate will suffer. try: lower reactivity in the master audio popover, drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover, or step the quality tier down; pick a simpler scene (spectrum or aurora instead of starfield); or open the image tab and disable fx shaders to remove a full-frame post-process pass. on laptops, make sure ikandy is using the discrete gpu: settings → system → display → graphics . the app won't launch / crashes on startup try a clean reinstall: uninstall via settings → apps, delete %appdata%\ikandy , then reinstall the latest build. if it still crashes, email support@ikandy.app with your windows version, gpu, and any error message shown. where are my settings stored? ikandy stores all user data in the electron userdata folder: %appdata%\ikandy (paste into the explorer address bar). files stored there include source preferences, preset reactivity scores, favorites, hidden presets, and thumbnail cache. uninstall note: the standard nsis uninstaller on windows does not delete %appdata%\ikandy . your settings, favorites, and cached thumbnails survive an uninstall and are picked up automatically when you reinstall. to fully reset ikandy, delete that folder manually after uninstalling. get help stuck? reach out. discord for chat and quick answers, email for bugs, coffee if it made your day. 💬 discord 🐛 report a bug ☕ support ← previous controls, themes, tips
